children.title: Circuit–Cocircuit Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between minimal dependence and minimal codependence.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C(M^{*})=\mathcal C^{*}(M)\) and \(\mathcal C^{*}(M^{*})=\mathcal C(M)\).

notation.meaning: family of circuits of the matroid
family of cocircuits of the matroid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit and cocircuit families on a common finite ground set.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cocircuit of \(M\) is, by definition, a circuit of \(M^{*}\). Therefore \[\mathcal C(M^{*})=\mathcal C^{*}(M),\qquad \mathcal C^{*}(M^{*})=\mathcal C(M).\] Equivalently, \(C^{*}\subseteq E\) is a cocircuit of \(M\) exactly when it is a minimal nonempty set meeting every basis of \(M\); it is then a circuit of the dual. Applying duality again exchanges the two incidence families back to their original roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Circuits of the dual are precisely cocircuits of the original matroid, and dual cocircuits are precisely original circuits.
knowledge_statements.title: Circuit–Cocircuit Duality

children.title: Flat–Hyperplane Duality

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\) is a hyperplane of \(M\) iff \(E\setminus H\) is a circuit of \(M^{*}\); \(F\) is a flat iff \(E\setminus F\) is a union of cocircuits of \(M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H\subseteq E\), \(H\) is a hyperplane of \(M\) if and only if \(E\setminus H\) is a cocircuit of \(M\), equivalently a circuit of \(M^{*}\). More generally, \(F\subseteq E\) is a flat of \(M\) if and only if, for every \(e\in E\setminus F\), there exists a cocircuit \(C^{*}\) of \(M\) satisfying \(e\in C^{*}\subseteq E\setminus F\). Thus \(E\setminus F\) is a union of cocircuits; the hyperplane case is exactly when this complement is one cocircuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hyperplane's complement is a cocircuit, hence a dual circuit; more generally, the complement of any flat is a union of cocircuits.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C\) is a circuit of \(M\) and \(D\) is a cocircuit of \(M\), then they cannot have exactly one common element: \[|C\cap D|\neq 1.\] Since cocircuits of \(M\) are circuits of \(M^{*}\), this is the fundamental incidence restriction between the primal and dual circuit systems. Equivalently, no circuit crosses the complement of a hyperplane in exactly one element. The statement permits disjoint intersections and intersections of cardinality at least two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A circuit and a cocircuit can be disjoint or meet several times, but they never intersect in exactly one element.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The class of finite transversal matroids is not closed under matroid duality. More precisely, if \(M\) is transversal, then \(M^{*}\) is a strict gammoid; conversely, the dual of every strict gammoid is transversal. Hence \[\{M^{*}:M\text{ is transversal}\}=\{N:N\text{ is a strict gammoid}\}.\] Since strict gammoids and transversal matroids are not the same class, one cannot infer that \(M^{*}\) is transversal merely from the transversality of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duals of transversal matroids are exactly strict gammoids, so the transversal class itself is not closed under duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Transversal Duality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed linkage and its associated bipartite graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directed linkage, linkage into a target set, the linkable-set family, and the bipartite construction used in transversal duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a directed graph with vertex set \(V\). Sets \(X,Y\subseteq V\) are linked if \(|X|=|Y|\) and there are \(|X|\) pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths whose initial vertices lie in \(X\) and whose final vertices lie in \(Y\); a path may consist of one vertex. The set \(X\) is linked into \(Z\subseteq V\) if it is linked to some subset of \(Z\), and \(L(G,B_0)=\{X\subseteq V:X\text{ is linked into }B_0\}\). For a disjoint copy \(\widehat V\) of \(V\), the associated bipartite graph \(\widehat G\) has vertex set \(V\cup\widehat V\) and edge set \(\{v\widehat v:v\in V\}\cup\{v\widehat u:(u,v)\in E(G)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equally sized vertex sets are linked when pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths join them, with one-vertex paths allowed. A set is linked into a target when it is linked to a subset of that target. The associated bipartite graph joins each vertex to its copy and joins v to the copy of u for every arc from u to v.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a directed graph with vertex set }V
\widehat V\text{ is a disjoint copy of }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(G,B_0)=\{X\subseteq V:X\text{ is linked into }B_0\},\qquad E(\widehat G)=\{v\widehat v:v\in V\}\cup\{v\widehat u:(u,v)\in E(G)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be represented over \(\mathbb F\) by a full-row-rank matrix whose columns are indexed by \(E\). After choosing a basis and permuting columns, write \(A=[I_r\ D]\). Then the matrix \[A^{*}=[-D^{\mathsf T}\ I_{|E|-r}]\] represents \(M^{*}\) over the same field, with columns in the corresponding complementary order. Indeed, the row spaces of \(A\) and \(A^{*}\) are orthogonal. Consequently, the class of matroids representable over any fixed field \(\mathbb F\) is closed under duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard-form matrix representation yields a transposed complementary matrix for the dual, so fixed-field representability is dual-closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Representable Duality

children.title: Dual-Closure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Class boundaries governing preservation or departure under dualization.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a class of finite matroids closed under isomorphism.
Duality is taken on the same ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is dual-closed iff \(M\in\mathcal K\Rightarrow M^{*}\in\mathcal K\); fixed-field representable classes satisfy this, while graphic and transversal classes generally do not.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure boundaries for common finite-matroid representation classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid class \(\mathcal K\) is dual-closed precisely when \(M\in\mathcal K\) implies \(M^{*}\in\mathcal K\). Matroids representable over a fixed field \(\mathbb F\) satisfy this condition. Graphic matroids do not satisfy it in general: their duals are cographic, becoming graphic in the planar regime. Transversal matroids also fail general dual closure: their duals are strict gammoids. Thus closure under duality must be established for the specified representation class and cannot be inferred merely from the existence of a primal representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-field representable matroids are dual-closed, whereas graphic and transversal matroids require larger dual partner classes except in special regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Closure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion of an arbitrary subset from a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid and let \(D\subseteq E\). The deletion of \(D\) from \(M\), denoted \(M\setminus D\), is the matroid on \(E\setminus D\) whose independent sets are
\[\mathcal I(M\setminus D)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq E\setminus D\}.\]
Equivalently, for every \(X\subseteq E\setminus D\), its rank satisfies \(r_{M\setminus D}(X)=r_M(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a subset removes its elements while retaining exactly the original independent sets supported on the remaining ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(M\setminus D)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq E\setminus D\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a finite matroid to a specified ground-set subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid and let \(S\subseteq E\). The restriction of \(M\) to \(S\), denoted \(M|S\), is the matroid on \(S\) with
\[\mathcal I(M|S)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq S\}.\]
Thus, for every \(X\subseteq S\), one has \(r_{M|S}(X)=r_M(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction retains a chosen subset and exactly those original independent sets contained in it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(M|S)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq S\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction characterized by its rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank function \(r_M\), and let \(C\subseteq E\). The contraction \(M/C\) is the matroid on \(E\setminus C\) whose rank function is
\[r_{M/C}(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\qquad(X\subseteq E\setminus C).\]
Equivalently, if \(B_C\) is any basis of \(M|C\), then \(I\subseteq E\setminus C\) is independent in \(M/C\) exactly when \(I\cup B_C\) is independent in \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contraction removes a subset after accounting for its rank; adjoining a basis of the contracted subset tests independence in the contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{M/C}(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\) for every \(X\subseteq E\setminus C\).

notation.meaning: a basis of the restriction to C

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Contraction by Dual Deletion

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid on \(E\) and let \(T\subseteq E\). The contraction of \(T\) from \(M\) is \[M/T=(M^*\setminus T)^*,\] with ground set \(E\setminus T\). It may also be denoted \(M.(E\setminus T)\), the contraction of \(M\) onto \(E\setminus T\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M/T=(M^*\setminus T)^*,\qquad E(M/T)=E\setminus T

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid contraction formulas
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual, rank, independence, and circuit descriptions of contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid and \(Z\subseteq S\). Contraction is defined by \(M/Z=(M^*\setminus Z)^*\). For every \(X\subseteq S\setminus Z\), \[r_{M/Z}(X)=r_M(X\cup Z)-r_M(Z).\] If \(B_Z\) is a base of \(Z\), then \(I\subseteq S\setminus Z\) is independent in \(M/Z\) if and only if \(I\cup B_Z\) is independent in \(M\). If \(Y=S\setminus Z\), the circuits of \(M/Z=M\cdot Y\) are precisely the inclusion-minimal nonempty sets among \(\{C\cap Y:C\in\mathcal C(M)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contraction is deletion in the dual followed by dualization. Its rank is obtained by adjoining the contracted set and subtracting its rank. Independence can be tested by adjoining a base of the contracted set, and its circuits are the minimal nonempty intersections of original circuits with the retained ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M/Z=(M^*\setminus Z)^*,\qquad r_{M/Z}(X)=r_M(X\cup Z)-r_M(Z),\qquad I\in\mathcal I(M/Z)\iff I\cup B_Z\in\mathcal I(M),\quad \mathcal C(M/Z)=\min_{\subseteq}\{C\cap(S\setminus Z)\ne\varnothing:C\in\mathcal C(M)\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion–Restriction Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equality between deletion and restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), and let \(D\subseteq E\). Deleting \(D\) is identical to restricting \(M\) to its complementary ground set:
\[M\setminus D=M|(E\setminus D).\]
The equality is literal as matroids on \(E\setminus D\): both sides have precisely the independent sets \(I\in\mathcal I(M)\) satisfying \(I\subseteq E\setminus D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a subset is exactly the same operation as restricting the matroid to the subset's complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\setminus D=M|(E\setminus D)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), let \(D,C\subseteq E\), and write \(M^*\) for its dual. Deletion and contraction are interchanged by duality:
\[(M\setminus D)^*=M^*/D,\qquad (M/C)^*=M^*\setminus C.\]
Each equality is between matroids on the corresponding complementary ground set. In particular, either minor operation can be defined from the other together with matroid duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the dual converts deletion into contraction and contraction into deletion on the same removed subset.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Deletion, Contraction, and Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-based definitions of deletion and contraction, followed by their interchange under dualization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(E,\mathcal I)$ have rank function $r$, and let $S\subseteq E$. The independent sets of $M\operatorname{del}S$ are the sets $I'\subseteq E\setminus S$ such that $r(I')=|I'|$. The independent sets of $M\operatorname{ctr}S$ are the sets $I''\subseteq E\setminus S$ such that $r(I''\cup S)=|I''|+r(S)$. Under matroid duality, deletion corresponds to contraction and contraction corresponds to deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion retains the independent sets disjoint from S. In the contraction by S, a disjoint set is independent exactly when adjoining it to S increases rank by the size of that set. Duality interchanges deletion and contraction.
assumptions_latex: M=(E,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I(M\operatorname{del}S)=\{I'\subseteq E\setminus S:r(I')=|I'|\},\quad \mathcal I(M\operatorname{ctr}S)=\{I''\subseteq E\setminus S:r(I''\cup S)=|I''|+r(S)\},\quad \text{duality interchanges deletion and contraction}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), and let \(C,D\subseteq E\) be disjoint. For the minor \(N=(M\setminus D)/C\), duality exchanges deletion and contraction:
\[N^*=(M^*/D)\setminus C.\]
Consequently, the dual of every minor of \(M\) is a minor of \(M^*\), with the deleted and contracted sets exchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of a minor is obtained from the dual matroid by exchanging its deleted and contracted sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duality of Matroid Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States invariance of the minor relation under matroid duality and the associated interchange of deletion and contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For matroids $M$ and $N$, $N$ is a minor of $M$ if and only if $N^*$ is a minor of $M^*$. More particularly, for disjoint $X,Y\subseteq E(M)$, $$N=M\setminus X/Y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N^*=M^*/X\setminus Y.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: N is a minor of M if and only if its dual is a minor of the dual of M. More particularly, duality changes deletion of X into contraction of X and contraction of Y into deletion of Y.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\preccurlyeq M\iff N^*\preccurlyeq M^*,\qquad N=M\setminus X/Y\iff N^*=M^*/X\setminus Y.

knowledge_statements.title: Minor Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction represented as projection of the rank and closure operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), contract \(C\subseteq E\), and put \(N=M/C\). For every \(X\subseteq E\setminus C\), the rank and closure in the projected matroid are
\[r_N(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C),\qquad \operatorname{cl}_N(X)=\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup C)\setminus C.\]
Thus contraction projects the dependence geometry of \(M\) along \(C\) onto the residual ground set \(E\setminus C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contracting a subset projects rank and closure onto the remaining ground set by adjoining the contracted subset before evaluating them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_N(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\) and \(\operatorname{cl}_N(X)=\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup C)\setminus C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scum Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction–restriction representation of an arbitrary matroid minor, with a flat contraction set when the minor is loopless.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be a minor of a matroid \(M\). Then there exists \(Z\subseteq E(M)\setminus E(N)\) such that \(M/Z\) and \(N\) have the same rank and \(N\) is a restriction of \(M/Z\). Moreover, if \(N\) has no loops, then \(Z\) can be chosen to be a flat of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every minor N of M is a restriction of a contraction M/Z having the same rank as N. If N is loopless, Z may be chosen as a flat of M.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists Z\subseteq E(M)\setminus E(N)\) such that \(r(M/Z)=r(N)\) and \(N\) is a restriction of \(M/Z\); if \(N\) is loopless, \(Z\) may be chosen flat in \(M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Transport through Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of flats under restriction and contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\). If \(S\subseteq E\), then the flats of \(M|S\) are exactly the sets \(F\cap S\), where \(F\) ranges over flats of \(M\). If \(C\subseteq E\), then a set \(G\subseteq E\setminus C\) is a flat of \(M/C\) exactly when \(G\cup C\) is a flat of \(M\). Hence restriction transports flats by intersection, while contraction transports them through flats containing the contracted set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction flats arise by intersection with the retained set; contraction flats correspond to original flats containing the contracted set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(M|S)=\{F\cap S:F\in\mathcal F(M)\}\) and \(G\in\mathcal F(M/C)\iff G\cup C\in\mathcal F(M)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flats under Contraction and Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact transport laws for flats through contraction and deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\subseteq E(M)\) and \(F\subseteq E(M)\setminus T\). Then (i) \(F\) is a flat of \(M/T\) if and only if \(F\cup T\) is a flat of \(M\); and (ii) \(F\) is a flat of \(M\setminus T\) if and only if there exists a flat \(F'\) of \(M\) such that \(F=F'\setminus T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set F disjoint from T is a flat after contracting T exactly when F union T is a flat of M. It is a flat after deleting T exactly when it is the part outside T of some flat of M.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in\mathcal L(M/T)\iff F\cup T\in\mathcal L(M)\), and \(F\in\mathcal L(M\setminus T)\iff \exists F'\in\mathcal L(M):F=F'\setminus T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Flat Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order correspondence between contraction flats and ambient flats above the contracted set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), let \(C\subseteq E\), and set \(N=M/C\). The maps
\[\Phi(G)=G\cup C,\qquad \Psi(F)=F\setminus C\]
are mutually inverse, inclusion-preserving bijections between the flats \(G\) of \(N\) and the flats \(F\) of \(M\) satisfying \(C\subseteq F\). Under this correspondence, the projected closure obeys \(\operatorname{cl}_N(X)=\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup C)\setminus C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flats of a contraction correspond bijectively, by adjoining or removing the contracted set, to original flats containing that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(N)\cong\{F\in\mathcal F(M):C\subseteq F\}\) via \(G\mapsto G\cup C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Minor-Closed Matroid Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of a matroid class under all finite minor operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A class \(\mathcal C\) of finite matroids is minor-closed if, for every \(M\in\mathcal C\) on ground set \(E\) and every pair of disjoint subsets \(C,D\subseteq E\),
\[(M\setminus D)/C\in\mathcal C.\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal C\) is closed separately under deletion and contraction. Since sequences of deletions and contractions can be reordered on disjoint sets, this condition contains every matroid minor of each member of \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid class is minor-closed when every deletion-contraction minor of each member remains in the class.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is a class of finite matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\in\mathcal C\) and \(C\cap D=\varnothing\) imply \((M\setminus D)/C\in\mathcal C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extremal matroid in a minor-closed class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines fixed-rank extension maximality and records that it is weaker than maximum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simple matroid \(M\) is extremal in a minor-closed class \(\mathcal M\) if \(M\in\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M\) contains no simple single-element extension of \(M\) having the same rank as \(M\). Every maximum-sized simple rank-\(r\) member of \(\mathcal M\) is extremal, but the converse is false. In particular, \(M^*(K_{3,3})\) is an extremal rank-4 regular matroid with nine elements, whereas the unique maximum-sized simple rank-4 regular matroid is \(M(K_5)\), with ten elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple matroid is extremal in a minor-closed class if it has no same-rank simple single-element extension within that class. Maximum size implies extremality, but not conversely; M*(K3,3) and M(K5) provide the stated rank-four regular-matroid example.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is a minor-closed class of matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is extremal in }\mathcal M\iff \nexists\,N\in\mathcal M\text{ that is a simple single-element extension of }M\text{ with }r(N)=r(M);\qquad \text{maximum-sized}\Rightarrow\text{extremal, but not conversely.}

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct sum of finite matroids on pairwise disjoint ground sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_1=(E_1,\mathcal I_1)\) and \(M_2=(E_2,\mathcal I_2)\) be finite matroids with \(E_1\cap E_2=\varnothing\). Their direct sum \(M_1\oplus M_2\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) with
\[\mathcal I(M_1\oplus M_2)=\{I_1\cup I_2:I_i\in\mathcal I_i\}.\]
Equivalently, for every \(X\subseteq E_1\cup E_2\),
\[r_{M_1\oplus M_2}(X)=r_{M_1}(X\cap E_1)+r_{M_2}(X\cap E_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sum combines disjoint matroids independently, so independent sets and ranks decompose componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(M_1\oplus M_2)=\{I_1\cup I_2:I_i\in\mathcal I_i\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contraction–restriction direct sum and compatible bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the bases of the direct sum of a contraction outside B and the restriction to B; the malformed trailing chain fragment is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a matroid on S, let B\subseteq S, and let \bar B=S\setminus B. Then M'=(M/B)\oplus(M\setminus\bar B) is a matroid on S, and its bases are exactly the bases K of M for which K\cap B is a basis of B in M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sum of the contraction by B and the restriction to B is a matroid on the original ground set. Its bases are precisely the original bases whose intersection with B is a basis of B.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal B\big((M/B)\oplus(M\setminus\bar B)\big)=\{K\in\mathcal B(M):K\cap B\text{ is a basis of }B\text{ in }M\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid classes closed under direct sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of standard representation and graph-derived matroid classes under binary direct sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) have disjoint ground sets. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct sum of matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite direct sums of matroids on pairwise disjoint ground sets, including the associated terminology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq 1\), and let \(M_1,\ldots,M_n\) be matroids on pairwise disjoint ground sets \(E_1,\ldots,E_n\). Their direct sum is \[M_1\oplus\cdots\oplus M_n=(E,\mathcal I),\qquad E=\bigcup_{i=1}^nE_i,\] where \[\mathcal I=\left\{\bigcup_{i=1}^n I_i:I_i\in\mathcal I(M_i)\text{ for every }i\right\}.\] For two summands this is also called a \(1\)-sum, and the \(M_i\) are called the direct-sum components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sum of finitely many matroids on pairwise disjoint ground sets has the union ground set and independent sets formed by taking one independent set from each summand. A binary direct sum is also called a 1-sum, and the summands are its direct-sum components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1\oplus\cdots\oplus M_n=\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^nE(M_i),\left\{\bigcup_{i=1}^n I_i:I_i\in\mathcal I(M_i)\ \forall i\right\}\right)

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit definition of the binary gluing operation along one ordinary element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_i\) be finite matroids on \(E_i\) with \(E_1\cap E_2=\{p\}\), where \(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either matroid. The two-sum \(M_1\oplus_2 M_2\) has ground set \((E_1\cup E_2)\setminus\{p\}\). Its circuits are the circuits of each \(M_i\) avoiding \(p\), together with all sets
\[(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\},\]
where \(C_i\) is a circuit of \(M_i\) containing \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sum glues two matroids along one nonloop, noncoloop element and then removes it, joining circuits that used the shared element.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either \(M_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C(M_1\oplus_2M_2)=\mathcal C_1^{\neg p}\cup\mathcal C_2^{\neg p}\cup\{(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\}:p\in C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i)\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid two-sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the matroid two-sum through series or parallel connection, including its hypotheses, symmetry, terminology, and minimum-size convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M and N be matroids such that |E(M)|,|E(N)|\ge 2, E(M)\cap E(N)=\{p\}, and \{p\} is not a separator of either M or N. The two-sum is M\oplus_2N:=S(M,N)/p=P(M,N)\setminus p. Moreover, N\oplus_2M=M\oplus_2N; p is the basepoint, and M and N are the parts. No requirement that each part have at least three elements is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two matroids with at least two elements that share exactly one element p, where p is not a one-element separator of either matroid, have a two-sum obtained by contracting p from their series connection, equivalently deleting p from their parallel connection. The operation is commutative, p is the basepoint, and the inputs are its parts. Parts need not have three elements.
assumptions_latex: \{p\}\text{ is not a separator of }M\text{ or }N
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\oplus_2N=S(M,N)/p=P(M,N)\setminus p=N\oplus_2M

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duality and connectivity of matroid two-sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records compatibility of two-sums with duality and the exact connectivity criterion for the deleted parallel connection and the resulting two-sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid two-sum M\oplus_2N, (M\oplus_2N)^*=M^*\oplus_2N^*. If |E(M)|,|E(N)|\ge 2, then P(M,N)\setminus p is connected if and only if both M and N are connected. In particular, M\oplus_2N is connected if and only if both M and N are connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing a matroid two-sum yields the two-sum of the dual matroids. For parts with at least two elements, deleting the basepoint from their parallel connection, and hence forming their two-sum, produces a connected matroid exactly when both parts are connected.
assumptions_latex: M\oplus_2N\text{ is a valid two-sum with basepoint }p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (M\oplus_2N)^*=M^*\oplus_2N^*,\qquad P(M,N)\setminus p\text{ is connected}\iff M\text{ and }N\text{ are connected},\qquad M\oplus_2N\text{ is connected}\iff M\text{ and }N\text{ are connected}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recovery of two-sum parts as minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States minor containment of both parts, an explicit recovery condition for M, and the sufficient size condition for properness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M\oplus_2N be a valid two-sum with basepoint p. Both M and N are isomorphic to minors of M\oplus_2N. If p'\in E(N)-\{p\} lies in the same component of N as p, then M can be obtained from a minor of M\oplus_2N by relabelling p' as p. If |E(N)|\ge 3, then M is isomorphic to a proper minor of M\oplus_2N.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both parts of a valid matroid two-sum occur, up to isomorphism, as minors of the sum. If an element p′ of N lies in the same component as the basepoint, an appropriate minor becomes M after p′ is relabelled as p. If N has at least three elements, M is isomorphic to a proper minor.
assumptions_latex: M\oplus_2N\text{ is a valid matroid two-sum with basepoint }p
p'\in E(N)-\{p\}\text{ lies in the same component of }N\text{ as }p\quad\text{for the explicit recovery claim}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M,N\preccurlyeq M\oplus_2N;\quad M\cong Q[p'\mapsto p]\text{ for some minor }Q\text{ under the stated condition};\quad |E(N)|\ge 3\Rightarrow M\text{ is isomorphic to a proper minor of }M\oplus_2N

\(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either matroid.
For the connectivity assertion, both \(M_i\) are connected and \(|E(M_i)|\ge 3\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite matroid \(M\), a partition \(E(M)=X\mathbin{\dot\cup}Y\) is a direct-sum separation exactly when \(\lambda_M(X)=0\), equivalently \(M=M|X\oplus M|Y\). If \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) satisfy the assumptions, their two-sum has ground set \((E(M_1)\cup E(M_2))\setminus\{p\}\) and bases \((B_1\cup B_2)\setminus\{p\}\), where each \(B_i\) is a basis of \(M_i\) and exactly one of \(B_1,B_2\) contains \(p\). The resulting two-sum is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct sums are exactly zero-connectivity separations. Gluing two connected matroids across a common nonloop, noncoloop and then deleting it produces a connected two-sum.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The parallel connection \(P(M_1,M_2)\) with basepoint \(p\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) whose circuits are the inclusion-minimal nonempty members of \[\mathcal C(M_1)\cup\mathcal C(M_2)\cup\{(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\}: C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i),\ p\in C_1\cap C_2\}.\] In particular, \(P(M_1,M_2)|E_i=M_i\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\), and the common element \(p\) remains in the ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parallel connection retains both matroids and adds circuits formed by joining one circuit from each side through their common nonloop basepoint.

children.top_down_role: Matroid composition across a larger shared restriction.

assumptions_latex: \(M_i\) is a finite matroid on \(E_i\), \(T=E_1\cap E_2\), and \(M_1|T=M_2|T=N\).
\(T\) is a modular semiflat of at least one of \(M_1,M_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum formula defines the generalized parallel connection \(P_N(M_1,M_2)\), an amalgam restricting to both input matroids.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(T\) is a modular semiflat of \(M_1\) when \(\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\) is modular and every element of \(\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\) is in \(T\), is a loop, or is parallel to an element of \(T\). Under the assumptions, the generalized parallel connection \(P_N(M_1,M_2)\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) with rank \[r_P(X)=\min_{Y:\,X\subseteq Y\subseteq E_1\cup E_2}\bigl(r_{M_1}(Y\cap E_1)+r_{M_2}(Y\cap E_2)-r_N(Y\cap T)\bigr).\] It satisfies \(P|E_i=M_i\) for \(i=1,2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible matroids can be amalgamated across a modular-semiflat common restriction; the proper-amalgam minimum formula gives the resulting rank function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural and minor laws of generalized parallel connections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constituent recovery, conditional symmetry, modularity, deletion, contraction, and interface-contraction laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=P_N(M_1,M_2)\). Then: (i) \(P\mid E_1=M_1\) and \(P\mid E_2=M_2\); (ii) if \(\operatorname{si}(T)\) is a modular flat in both \(\operatorname{si}(M_1)\) and \(\operatorname{si}(M_2)\), then \(P_N(M_2,M_1)=P_N(M_1,M_2)\); (iii) \(E(\operatorname{si}(M_2))\) is a modular flat of \(\operatorname{si}(P)\); (iv) if \(e\in E_1\setminus T\), then \(P\setminus e=P_N(M_1\setminus e,M_2)\); (v) if \(e\in E_1\setminus\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\), then \(P/e=P_N(M_1/e,M_2)\); (vi) if \(e\in E_2\setminus T\), then \(P\setminus e=P_N(M_1,M_2\setminus e)\); (vii) if \(e\in E_2\setminus\operatorname{cl}_{M_2}(T)\), then \(P/e=P_N(M_1,M_2/e)\); (viii) if \(e\in T\), then \(P/e=P_{N/e}(M_1/e,M_2/e)\); and (ix) \(P/T=(M_1/T)\oplus(M_2/T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized parallel connection recovers both constituents by restriction, is symmetric under the stated two-sided modularity condition, has the stated modular-flat property, commutes with deletion and the specified contractions, and becomes a direct sum after contracting the whole interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ satisfies properties (i)--(ix), with the stated clause-specific hypotheses.}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized parallel connection across a modular common restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the construction and records the accompanying rank formula for its flats.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=M_1\mid T=M_2\mid T\), define \(\operatorname{si}(T)=\operatorname{si}(M_1\mid T)\), and suppose \(\operatorname{si}(T)\) is a modular flat of \(\operatorname{si}(M_1)\). For every flat \(F\) of this matroid, \[r(F)=r(F\cap E_1)+r(F\cap E_2)-r(F\cap T).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the simplified common restriction is a modular flat of the simplification of M1, the proper amalgam is called the generalized parallel connection across T. children.title: Connection Interface Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions on shared restrictions supporting connection constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Agreement on \(T\) is necessary; a modular-semiflat interface is sufficient for the canonical proper amalgam, while arbitrary compatible interfaces need not admit one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary compatibility and standard sufficient interface condition.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An amalgam \(P\) on \(E(M_1)\cup E(M_2)\) satisfying \(P|E(M_i)=M_i\) can exist only if the two restrictions to the overlap agree: \(M_1|T=M_2|T\). Agreement alone does not guarantee existence or uniqueness. A standard sufficient regime is that \(T\) be a modular semiflat of at least one input matroid; then the proper-amalgam rank formula defines the canonical generalized parallel connection \(P_N(M_1,M_2)\). Thus interface compatibility is necessary, while modular-semiflat structure supplies the additional rank consistency needed by this construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inputs must agree on their overlap. A modular-semiflat overlap guarantees the canonical generalized parallel connection; mere agreement may not guarantee any amalgam or uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Connection Interface Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient condition for full embedding and proper amalgam existence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An interface criterion in the common-restriction setup for amalgamating matroids across T.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the amalgam setup for \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) across \(T\), suppose \(\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\) is a modular flat of \(M_1\), and every nonloop element of \(\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\setminus T\) is parallel to an element of \(T\). Then \(T\) is fully embedded in \(M_1\), so the proper amalgam of \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the closure of T in M1 is modular and every nonloop element added by the closure is parallel to an element of T, then T is fully embedded in M1 and the proper amalgam exists.
assumptions_latex: \(\forall e\in\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\setminus T,\ e\text{ nonloop}\Rightarrow\exists t\in T\text{ parallel to }e\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{ is fully embedded in }M_1\), and the proper amalgam of \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular defect and fully embedded subsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of modular defect and the fully embedded interface condition; the accompanying example is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid with rank function \(r\). For \(X,Y\subseteq E(M)\), define \(\delta(X,Y)=r(X)+r(Y)-r(X\cup Y)-r(X\cap Y)\). A subset \(Z\subseteq E(M)\) is fully embedded in \(M\) if \(\delta(F_1\cap Z,F_2\cap Z)\leq\delta(F_1,F_2)\) for all flats \(F_1,F_2\) of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The modular defect measures the slack in the rank submodularity inequality. A subset is fully embedded when intersecting any two flats with it does not increase their modular defect.
assumptions_latex: \(M\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta(X,Y):=r(X)+r(Y)-r(X\cup Y)-r(X\cap Y),\qquad Z\text{ is fully embedded}\iff \forall F_1,F_2,\ \delta(F_1\cap Z,F_2\cap Z)\leq\delta(F_1,F_2).\)

children.title: Parallel-Connection Specialization
children.top_down_role: Placement of ordinary parallel connection within the generalized construction.

assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are finite matroids, \(E_i=E(M_i)\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\), and \(E_1\cap E_2=\{p\}\).
\(p\) is not a loop of either matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized parallel connection over \(N=U_{1,1}\) equals the ordinary parallel connection: \(P_N(M_1,M_2)=P(M_1,M_2)\).

notation.meaning: Ground set of the input matroid M_i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singleton-interface specialization of generalized parallel connection.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Both restrictions to \(\{p\}\) equal \(N=U_{1,1}\), and the singleton interface is a modular semiflat. For every \(X\subseteq E_1\cup E_2\), the generalized parallel connection has rank \[r_{P_N(M_1,M_2)}(X)=\min_{Y:\,X\subseteq Y\subseteq E_1\cup E_2}\bigl(r_{M_1}(Y\cap E_1)+r_{M_2}(Y\cap E_2)-r_N(Y\cap\{p\})\bigr).\] The matroid defined by this specialization is the ordinary parallel connection, so \(P_N(M_1,M_2)=P(M_1,M_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the common restriction is one nonloop element, the generalized parallel-connection rank formula specializes exactly to the ordinary parallel connection.

children.title: Single-Element Extensions
children.top_down_role: Matroid enlargement by one new element.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single-element extension is exactly a matroid \(M'\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) satisfying \(M'\setminus e=M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite single-element extension, including loop and coloop cases.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-element extension of \(M\) by \(e\) is a matroid \(M'\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) such that \(M'\setminus e=M\). Equivalently, \(r_{M'}(X)=r_M(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq E\), while for each \(X\subseteq E\), \(r_{M'}(X\cup\{e\})\) is either \(r_M(X)\) or \(r_M(X)+1\), consistently with the matroid rank axioms. The extension is a loop extension when \(e\in\operatorname{cl}_{M'}(\varnothing)\) and a coloop extension when \(r(M')=r(M)+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-element extension adds one element whose deletion recovers the original matroid; its rank contribution over each old subset is zero or one.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Element Extensions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Extensions and Single-Element Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines matroid extension by deletion and its one-element specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be matroids. If \(M=N\setminus T\) for some nonempty set \(T\subseteq E(N)\), then \(N\) is an extension of \(M\). If \(|T|=1\), then \(N\) is a single-element extension of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid N is an extension of M if deleting a nonempty subset T from N yields M. It is a single-element extension when T contains exactly one element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\text{ is an extension of }M;\qquad |T|=1\Rightarrow N\text{ is a single-element extension of }M.

children.title: Single-Element Coextensions
children.top_down_role: Dual enlargement associated with single-element extensions.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single-element coextension is exactly a matroid \(N\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) satisfying \(N/e=M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite coextension defined through contraction and dual extension.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-element coextension of \(M\) by \(e\) is a matroid \(N\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) such that \(N/e=M\). Equivalently, duality converts the construction into an extension: \(N\) is a coextension of \(M\) if and only if \(N^*\setminus e=M^*\). Thus cocircuits and corank behavior of a coextension are obtained by applying the circuit and rank description of a single-element extension to the dual matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coextension adds one element whose contraction recovers the original matroid; equivalently, its dual is a single-element extension of the dual matroid.

children.title: Modular-Cut Encoding
children.top_down_role: Encoding of extension choices through modular cuts in the flat lattice.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Modular cuts of \(M\) are in bijection with single-element extensions of \(M\) on a fixed new element.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical modular-cut encoding of finite one-element extensions.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A modular cut is a collection \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal F(M)\) that is upward closed among flats and satisfies: if \(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal C\) and \(r(F_1)+r(F_2)=r(F_1\cap F_2)+r(F_1\cup F_2)\), then \(F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal C\). For an extension \(M'\) by \(e\), its cut is \(\mathcal C_e=\{F\in\mathcal F(M):e\in\operatorname{cl}_{M'}(F)\}\). Conversely, \(\mathcal C\) determines the extension through \[r_{M'}(X\cup\{e\})=\begin{cases}r_M(X),&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\in\mathcal C,\\r_M(X)+1,&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\notin\mathcal C.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modular cut records exactly which old flats span the new element, and this data uniquely determines the single-element extension rank function.
knowledge_statements.title: Modular-Cut Encoding

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular Cut of a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a modular cut and records the modular cuts induced by the loop and coloop extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\mathcal M\) of flats of a matroid \(M\) is a modular cut if: (i) whenever \(F\in\mathcal M\) and \(F'\) is a flat of \(M\) containing \(F\), then \(F'\in\mathcal M\); and (ii) whenever \(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal M\) form a modular pair, then \(F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal M\). Every single-element extension induces a modular cut. The extensions \(M\oplus U_{0,1}\) and \(M\oplus U_{1,1}\) induce, respectively, the family of all flats of \(M\) and the empty family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modular cut is an upward-closed family of flats closed under intersections of modular pairs. Every single-element extension induces one; adding a loop yields all flats, while adding a coloop yields the empty family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a modular cut}\iff\left[\begin{array}{l}F\in\mathcal M,\ F\subseteq F',\ F'\in\mathcal F(M)\Rightarrow F'\in\mathcal M,\\F_1,F_2\in\mathcal M\text{ form a modular pair}\Rightarrow F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal M\end{array}\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Single-Element Extension Represented by a Modular Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the unique extension represented by a modular cut and gives its rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid on \(E\), let \(\mathcal M\) be a modular cut of \(M\), and let \(e\notin E\). There is a unique extension \(N\) of \(M\) on \(E\dot\cup\{e\}\) such that \(\mathcal M\) is exactly the set of flats \(F\) of \(M\) for which \(F\cup\{e\}\) is a flat of \(N\) having rank \(r_M(F)\). For every \(X\subseteq E\), \(r_N(X)=r_M(X)\) and \[r_N(X\cup\{e\})=\begin{cases}r_M(X),&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\in\mathcal M,\\r_M(X)+1,&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\notin\mathcal M.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every modular cut determines a unique single-element extension. Old subsets retain their ranks; adjoining the new element preserves rank exactly when the old subset's closure belongs to the modular cut, and otherwise raises rank by one.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a modular cut of }M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!N\text{ on }E\dot\cup\{e\}\text{ with }N\setminus e=M,\quad r_N(X)=r_M(X),\quad r_N(X\cup\{e\})=\begin{cases}r_M(X),&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\in\mathcal M,\\r_M(X)+1,&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\notin\mathcal M\end{cases}\ \forall X\subseteq E.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular-Cut Properties Induced by a Single-Element Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the upward-closure and modular-pair intersection properties of the flat family induced by an extension element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\setminus e=M\), and let \(\mathcal M\) be the set of flats \(F\) of \(M\) such that \(F\cup\{e\}\) is a flat of \(N\) and \(r_N(F\cup\{e\})=r_M(F)\). Then: (i) if \(F\in\mathcal M\) and \(F'\) is a flat of \(M\) containing \(F\), then \(F'\in\mathcal M\); and (ii) if \(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal M\) form a modular pair, then \(F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relevant flats of a single-element extension form an upward-closed family, and the intersection of any modular pair in that family also belongs to it.
assumptions_latex: N\text{ is a matroid and }N\setminus e=M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(F\in\mathcal M,\ F\subseteq F',\ F'\in\mathcal F(M)\bigr)\Rightarrow F'\in\mathcal M;\qquad \bigl(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal M\text{ form a modular pair}\bigr)\Rightarrow F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal M.

children.title: Extension–Coextension Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between extension and coextension regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\setminus e=M\) if and only if \(N^*/e=M^*\), and \(N/e=M\) if and only if \(N^*\setminus e=M^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion–contraction duality for one-element constructions.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Matroid duality exchanges deletion and contraction: \((N\setminus e)^*=N^*/e\) and \((N/e)^*=N^*\setminus e\). Consequently, \(N\) is a single-element extension of \(M\) exactly when \(N^*\) is a single-element coextension of \(M^*\), and \(N\) is a single-element coextension of \(M\) exactly when \(N^*\) is a single-element extension of \(M^*\). The correspondence is involutive because \((M^*)^*=M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality exchanges single-element extensions with coextensions because it exchanges deletion with contraction.
knowledge_statements.title: Extension–Coextension Duality

children.title: Extension Realizability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on admissible extension data.

assumptions_latex: \(A=(a_x)_{x\in E}\) represents \(M\) over a field \(\mathbb F\) in a vector space \(V\).
\(W\) is a vector space containing \(V\), and \(v\in W\) represents a proposed new element \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An extension preserving the fixed representation is realizable exactly when its modular cut equals \(\{F:v\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F}\{a_x:x\in F\}\}\) for some \(W\supseteq V\) and \(v\in W\).

notation.meaning: Linear span over the representation field

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability relative to a fixed linear representation and field.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Appending \(v\) to \(A\) produces a represented extension whose modular cut is \[\mathcal C_v=\{F\in\mathcal F(M):v\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F}\{a_x:x\in F\}\}.\] Conversely, every extension that extends this fixed representation arises from such a vector in some ambient \(W\supseteq V\). Therefore an abstract modular cut need not be realizable over \(\mathbb F\) relative to \(A\): realizability fails precisely when no vector has the prescribed incidences with the spans of all flats. Allowing \(v\notin V\) includes the coloop extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed linear representation, realizable extensions are exactly modular cuts induced by one vector’s membership in flat spans; other modular cuts are unrealizable there.
knowledge_statements.title: Extension Realizability Boundaries

children.title: Matroid Quotients
children.top_down_role: Strong-map quotient relationships between matroids.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(Q\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) exactly when every flat of \(Q\) is a flat of \(M\).

notation.meaning: Deletion and contraction of an auxiliary set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-map definition and common-minor characterization of finite quotients.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) when the identity map on \(E\) is a strong map from \(M\) to \(Q\), equivalently when \(\mathcal F(Q)\subseteq\mathcal F(M)\). For finite matroids this is also equivalent to the existence of a matroid \(L\) on \(E\mathbin{\dot\cup}X\), for some finite auxiliary set \(X\), such that \(M=L\setminus X\) and \(Q=L/X\). Thus contraction of the auxiliary elements modifies rank while retaining the same displayed ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quotient has no flats beyond those of the original matroid; equivalently, both arise as deletion and contraction of the same auxiliary elements.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Quotients

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent-set representation of matroid quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes quotients through deletion and contraction of an independent set in a rank-preserving ambient matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(Q\) is a quotient of a matroid \(M\) if and only if there exist a matroid \(N\) with \(r(N)=r(M)\) and an independent set \(I\) of \(N\) such that \[M=N\setminus I\qquad\text{and}\qquad Q=N/I.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Q is a quotient of M exactly when some matroid N of the same rank as M contains an independent set I whose deletion gives M and whose contraction gives Q.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\text{ is a quotient of }M\iff \exists N,I:\ r(N)=r(M),\ I\text{ is independent in }N,\ M=N\setminus I,\ Q=N/I.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid quotients and elementary quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines general and elementary matroid quotients and records the excluded trivial modular-cut cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid and let \(\mathcal M\) be a nonempty proper modular cut of \(M\). The elementary quotient of \(M\) with respect to \(\mathcal M\) is \((M+_{\mathcal M}e)/e\); it has ground set \(E(M)\) and rank \(r(M)-1\). More generally, \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) if there exist a matroid \(N\) and a set \(X\subseteq E(N)\) such that \(M=N\setminus X\) and \(Q=N/X\). Consequently, \(E(Q)=E(M)\). If \(\mathcal M\) is empty or is the set of all flats of \(M\), the elementary construction instead returns \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elementary quotient is obtained by extending a matroid using a nonempty proper modular cut and then contracting the new element; it preserves the ground set and lowers rank by one. In general, Q is a quotient of M when deleting a set X from some matroid N gives M while contracting X gives Q. Empty or nonproper modular cuts produce only the trivial result M.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a nonempty proper modular cut of }M
\text{For the general definition, }N\text{ is a matroid and }X\subseteq E(N)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (M+_{\mathcal M}e)/e\text{ is an elementary quotient of rank }r(M)-1;\quad Q\text{ is a quotient of }M\iff \exists N,X:\ M=N\setminus X,\ Q=N/X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of matroid quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the quotient relation on a common ground set through flats, rank increments, circuits, and closures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1,M_2\) be matroids on a common ground set \(E\), with rank functions \(r_1,r_2\) and closure operators \(\operatorname{cl}_1,\operatorname{cl}_2\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(M_2\) is a quotient of \(M_1\); (ii) every flat of \(M_2\) is a flat of \(M_1\); (iii) for all \(X\subseteq Y\subseteq E\), \(r_1(Y)-r_1(X)\ge r_2(Y)-r_2(X)\); (iv) every circuit of \(M_1\) is a union of circuits of \(M_2\); and (v) for every \(X\subseteq E\), \(\operatorname{cl}_1(X)\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_2(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two matroids on the same ground set, M2 is a quotient of M1 exactly when each of four equivalent structural conditions holds: every flat of M2 is a flat of M1; rank increments in M1 dominate those in M2 for every nested pair of sets; every circuit of M1 is a union of circuits of M2; and the M1-closure of every set is contained in its M2-closure.
assumptions_latex: M_1\text{ and }M_2\text{ are matroids on the common ground set }E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}M_2\text{ is a quotient of }M_1&\iff \operatorname{Flats}(M_2)\subseteq\operatorname{Flats}(M_1)\\&\iff \forall X\subseteq Y\subseteq E,\ r_1(Y)-r_1(X)\ge r_2(Y)-r_2(X)\\&\iff \text{every circuit of }M_1\text{ is a union of circuits of }M_2\\&\iff \forall X\subseteq E,\ \operatorname{cl}_1(X)\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_2(X).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorization of a quotient into elementary quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a quotient of rank difference k as a chain of exactly k elementary quotients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) and \(Q\) be matroids and let \(k=r(M)-r(Q)\). Then \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) if and only if there exist matroids \(M_0,M_1,\ldots,M_k\) such that \(M_0=M\), \(M_k=Q\), and, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(M_i\) is an elementary quotient of \(M_{i-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the rank difference between M and Q is k, then Q is a quotient of M exactly when M can be transformed into Q through a chain of k elementary quotients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\text{ is a quotient of }M\iff \exists(M_i)_{i=0}^k:\ M_0=M,\ M_k=Q,\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\ M_i\text{ is an elementary quotient of }M_{i-1}.

children.top_down_role: Lift relationships dual to quotient structure.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(L\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) is a lift of \(M\) exactly when \(M\) is a quotient of \(L\), equivalently when \(L^*\) is a quotient of \(M^*\).

notation.meaning: Deletion and contraction of auxiliary elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite lifts as reverse quotients, with dual characterization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(L\) is a lift of \(M\) if \(M\) is a quotient of \(L\). Equivalently, there exist a finite set \(X\) disjoint from \(E\) and a matroid \(K\) on \(E\mathbin{\dot\cup}X\) such that \(L=K\setminus X\) and \(M=K/X\). By deletion–contraction duality, this holds if and only if \(L^*\) is a quotient of \(M^*\). In flat language, the quotient relation gives \(\mathcal F(M)\subseteq\mathcal F(L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift reverses the quotient relation: deleting auxiliary elements gives the lift, while contracting them gives the original matroid; duality converts lifts back to quotients.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Lifts

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid lifts, their representation, and dual characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines lifts and elementary lifts, represents a lift by deletion and contraction from a common matroid, and gives the dual quotient equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(M_1\) is a lift of \(M_2\) when \(M_2\) is a quotient of \(M_1\); if \(M_2\) is an elementary quotient of \(M_1\), then \(M_1\) is an elementary lift of \(M_2\). Moreover, \(M_1\) is a lift of \(M_2\) if and only if there exist a matroid \(N\) and \(Y\subseteq E(N)\) such that \(N\setminus Y=M_1\) and \(N/Y=M_2\). Equivalently, \(M_1\) is a lift of \(M_2\) if and only if \(M_1^*\) is a quotient of \(M_2^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift reverses the quotient relation. The two matroids can be obtained from a common matroid by deleting and contracting the same set, and dualizing converts the lift relation into a quotient relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1\text{ is a lift of }M_2\iff \exists N\,\exists Y\subseteq E(N):\ N\setminus Y=M_1\ \land\ N/Y=M_2\iff M_1^*\text{ is a quotient of }M_2^*

children.title: Matroid Truncations
children.top_down_role: Rank-lowering construction preserving lower-cardinality independence.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Truncations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rank truncation of a finite matroid by an integer threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid with rank function \(r_M\), and let \(k\) satisfy \(0\le k\le r_M(E)\). The rank-\(k\) truncation \(T_k(M)\) is the matroid on \(E\) whose independent sets and rank function are
\[\mathcal I(T_k(M))=\{I\in\mathcal I:|I|\le k\},\qquad r_{T_k(M)}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),k\}\quad(X\subseteq E).\]
Its bases are exactly the independent \(k\)-subsets of \(M\). The ordinary truncation is \(T_{r_M(E)-1}(M)\) when \(r_M(E)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncation caps every set's rank at k; its independent sets are precisely the original independent sets having at most k elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{T_k(M)}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),k\}\) for every \(X\subseteq E\).

children.title: Free Extensions
children.top_down_role: Generic single-element extension regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Free Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the one-element free extension, including the rank-zero convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid of rank \(r\), and let \(e\notin E\). The free extension \(M+e\) is the matroid on \(E\cup\{e\}\) with independent sets
\[\mathcal I(M+e)=\mathcal I\cup\{J\cup\{e\}:J\in\mathcal I,\ |J|<r\}.\]
Thus deletion of \(e\) returns \(M\), while \(e\) lies in the closure of \(E\) but in the closure of no nonspanning subset of \(E\). If \(r=0\), the new element is a loop under this convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free extension adds an element that can augment every nonspanning independent set but does not increase the matroid's total rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid of rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M+e)\setminus e=M\) and \(r(M+e)=r(M)\).

notation.meaning: free extension of M by e

children.title: Quotient–Lift Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between quotient and lift constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient–Lift Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States deletion–contraction duality for quotient and lift relations on a common ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) and \(N\) be finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\). Say that \(N\) is a quotient of \(M\) if there exist a finite set \(X\) disjoint from \(E\) and a matroid \(L\) on \(E\cup X\) such that \(M=L\setminus X\) and \(N=L/X\); equivalently, \(M\) is a lift of \(N\). Since duality interchanges deletion and contraction,
\[N\text{ is a quotient of }M\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N^*\text{ is a lift of }M^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality reverses the quotient relation: N is a quotient of M exactly when the dual of N is a lift of the dual of M.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(N\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is a quotient of \(M\) if and only if \(N^*\) is a lift of \(M^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quotient relation reverses under matroid duality: M1 is a quotient of M2 exactly when the dual of M2 is a quotient of the dual of M1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1\text{ is a quotient of }M_2\iff M_2^*\text{ is a quotient of }M_1^*.

children.title: Truncation–Free-Extension Relation
children.top_down_role: Structural connection between truncation and free-extension regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncation–Free-Extension Relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents ordinary truncation as contraction of a freely added element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank \(r>0\), and let \(M+e\) be its free extension by an element \(e\notin E\). Then
\[(M+e)/e=T_{r-1}(M).\]
Equivalently, its rank function satisfies
\[r_{(M+e)/e}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),r-1\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
Thus every ordinary truncation of a positive-rank matroid has a free-extension-and-contraction representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freely adding one element to a positive-rank matroid and then contracting it produces the original matroid truncated by one rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank \(r>0\).

notation.meaning: free extension of M by e

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Binary matroids, regular matroids, and total unimodularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparative definitions of two representable-matroid classes and the matrix property used to define regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid is binary if it is representable over $\operatorname{GF}(2)$. A real matrix is totally unimodular if every square submatrix has determinant in $\{0,1,-1\}$. A matroid is regular if it can be represented by a totally unimodular matrix; such matroids are also called unimodular matroids by some authors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary matroid is representable over GF(2). A real matrix is totally unimodular when every square submatrix has determinant 0, 1, or -1. A regular matroid has a totally unimodular matrix representation and is also sometimes called a unimodular matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is binary}\iff M\text{ is representable over }\operatorname{GF}(2),\qquad M\text{ is regular}\iff M\text{ has a totally unimodular matrix representation}.

children.title: Uniform Matroids
children.top_down_role: Cardinality-bounded canonical matroids.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite uniform matroid by a single global cardinality capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite set \(E\) of cardinality \(n\) and an integer \(r\) with \(0\le r\le n\), the uniform matroid \(U_{r,n}\) has independent sets
\[\mathcal I(U_{r,n})=\{I\subseteq E:|I|\le r\}.\]
Consequently every \(r\)-subset is a basis, every subset of size at most \(r\) is independent, and its rank function is
\[r_{U_{r,n}}(X)=\min\{|X|,r\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uniform matroid of rank r declares every subset of at most r elements independent and every larger subset dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(U_{r,n})=\{I\subseteq E:|I|\le r\}\).

notation.meaning: uniform matroid of rank r on n elements

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The cardinality-bounded independent-set definition of a uniform matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an n-element ground set, declaring exactly the subsets of size at most k independent defines the rank-k uniform matroid U_n^k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(S,\{I\subseteq S:|I|\le k\}\right)=U_n^k\text{ is a matroid of rank }k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties of the uniform matroid U_{2,4}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Class, representability, duality, connectivity, roundedness, and algebraicity properties of the four-point line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The uniform matroid $U_{2,4}$ is the four-point line and is isomorphic to the rank-two whirl $\mathcal W^2$. It is the unique excluded minor for binary matroids and an excluded minor for graphic, cographic, and regular matroids. It is $\mathbb F$-representable if and only if $|\mathbb F|\ge 3$, and it is near-regular. It is transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid, identically self-dual, and algebraic over every field, and its automorphism group is the symmetric group. It is also the unique three-connected nonbinary matroid $M$ having an element $e$ such that both $M\setminus e$ and $M/e$ are binary, and the unique matroid $M$ with at least four elements such that $\{M\}$ is 2-rounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: U(2,4), the four-point line, is the rank-two whirl. It has the stated excluded-minor, field-representability, class-membership, duality, automorphism, connectivity, roundedness, and algebraicity properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_{2,4}\cong\mathcal W^2\text{ and has all the stated properties.}

children.title: Partition Matroids
children.top_down_role: Block-capacity matroids induced by a ground-set partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines partition matroids through disjoint block-capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E=E_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_m\) be a partition of a finite set, and choose integer capacities \(0\le b_i\le |E_i|\). The associated partition matroid has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap E_i|\le b_i\text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\]
Its rank function is
\[r(X)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\min\{|X\cap E_i|,b_i\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
Thus feasibility is determined independently within each block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition matroid permits at most a prescribed number of selected elements from each block of a partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is independent exactly when \(|I\cap E_i|\le b_i\) for every \(i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit-Capacity Partition Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition matroids whose block capacities are all one, including the stated disjoint-star representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=U_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}U_k\) be a partition. The associated unit-capacity partition matroid has independent-set family \(\mathcal I=\{U'\subseteq U:|U'\cap U_i|\leq 1\text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,k\}\). In the stated bipartite special case, every vertex of \(U\) has degree one, so the star components induce the blocks \(U_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit-capacity partition matroid permits an independent set to contain at most one element from each block. In the stated bipartite construction, degree-one vertices form disjoint star components that induce those blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U'\in\mathcal I\iff |U'\cap U_i|\leq 1\quad\text{for all }i=1,\ldots,k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit-capacity partition matroid and its rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the partition matroid having capacity one on every block and gives its direct-sum representation and rank formula.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=(S,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid and }r(A)=|\{i:A\cap S_i\neq\varnothing\}|\quad\forall A\subseteq S.

children.title: Laminar Matroids
children.top_down_role: Capacity matroids induced by a laminar set family.

knowledge_statements.title: Laminar Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite laminar matroids using capacities on nested-or-disjoint subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite and let \(\mathcal L\subseteq 2^E\) be laminar: for all \(A,B\in\mathcal L\), either \(A\subseteq B\), \(B\subseteq A\), or \(A\cap B=\varnothing\). Assign each \(A\in\mathcal L\) an integer capacity \(0\le b(A)\le |A|\). The laminar matroid determined by \((\mathcal L,b)\) has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap A|\le b(A)\text{ for every }A\in\mathcal L\}.\]
The laminar nesting condition is what guarantees the matroid exchange axiom for these simultaneous capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A laminar matroid imposes cardinality capacities on a family of subsets in which every two sets are nested or disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap A|\le b(A)\ \forall A\in\mathcal L\}\) is a matroid independence system.

children.title: Capacity-Class Specializations
children.top_down_role: Containment and specialization relationships among uniform, partition, and laminar classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Class Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the nesting of global, partition, and laminar capacity matroid classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Finite cardinality-capacity matroids admit the specialization chain
\[\{\text{uniform matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{partition matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{laminar matroids}\}.\]
Specifically, \(U_{r,n}\) is the partition matroid with the single block \(E\) and capacity \(r\). A partition matroid with blocks \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) and capacities \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\) is the laminar matroid with \(\mathcal L=\{E_1,\ldots,E_m\}\) and \(b(E_i)=b_i\). Adding nested sets to \(\mathcal L\) yields capacities shared across several descendant blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform matroids are one-block partition matroids, and partition matroids are laminar matroids whose constrained sets are pairwise disjoint.
assumptions_latex: All ground sets and capacity families are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{Uniform}\subseteq\mathrm{Partition}\subseteq\mathrm{Laminar}\).

children.top_down_role: Matroid classes induced by schedulability constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the unit-time, single-machine deadline-feasibility version of a scheduling matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite set of unit-processing-time jobs, each with an integer deadline \(d_j\ge1\), to be scheduled without idle-time restrictions on one machine starting at time zero. Define
\[\mathcal I=\left\{I\subseteq E:\left|\{j\in I:d_j\le t\}\right|\le t\text{ for every integer }t\ge1\right\}.\]
Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid. Its independent sets are exactly the job subsets admitting an ordering in which every job completes no later than its deadline; earliest-deadline-first provides such an ordering whenever the inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit-time jobs with deadlines form a matroid: a subset is independent exactly when it can be scheduled on one machine without missing a deadline.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite collection of unit-time jobs.
Each deadline \(d_j\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is schedulable by its deadlines if and only if \(|\{j\in I:d_j\le t\}|\le t\) for all integers \(t\ge1\).

children.title: Count Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids governed by subset-count capacity constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Count Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard vertex-weighted graphical count-matroid construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless graph, let \(m:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and let \(\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) satisfy \(m(u)+m(v)\ge\ell+1\) for every edge \(uv\in E\). For \(F\subseteq E\), write \(V(F)\) for its incident vertices. The count matroid has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le m(V(F'))-\ell\text{ for every nonempty }F'\subseteq F\},\]
where \(m(X)=\sum_{v\in X}m(v)\). Under the stated edge condition, this system satisfies the matroid axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graphical count matroid bounds every nonempty edge subset by the total weights of its incident vertices minus a fixed offset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I=\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le m(V(F'))-\ell\ \forall\varnothing\ne F'\subseteq F\}\) is a matroid independence system.

children.title: Sparsity Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids arising from sparsity constraints on combinatorial structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite graphical sparsity matroids in the standard integer parameter range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless graph, let \(k\ge1\), and let \(0\le\ell\le2k-1\) be integers. An edge set \(F\subseteq E\) is \((k,\ell)\)-sparse when every nonempty \(F'\subseteq F\) satisfies
\[|F'|\le k|V(F')|-\ell.\]
The family of all \((k,\ell)\)-sparse subsets of \(E\) is the independent-set family of the \((k,\ell)\)-sparsity matroid of \(G\). A spanning set is \((k,\ell)\)-tight when it is sparse and has \(|F|=k|V|-\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity matroid declares an edge set independent when every nonempty subcollection has at most k times its incident-vertex count minus l edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le k|V(F')|-\ell\ \forall\varnothing\ne F'\subseteq F\}\) is a matroid independence system.

children.title: Constraint-Generation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating matroidal constraint systems from nonmatroidal ones.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Generation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that arbitrary overlapping cardinality constraints need not define a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E=\{1,2,3\}\) and impose the two capacities
\[|I\cap\{1,2\}|\le1,\qquad |I\cap\{2,3\}|\le1.\]
The resulting hereditary family contains \(A=\{2\}\) and \(B=\{1,3\}\), with \(|A|<|B|\). However, neither \(A\cup\{1\}\) nor \(A\cup\{3\}\) is feasible. Hence the augmentation axiom fails, so arbitrary overlapping capacity sets do not necessarily generate a matroid. Structural hypotheses such as disjointness, laminarity, or an appropriate submodular count construction are therefore essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two crossing capacity constraints on three elements yield a hereditary system that violates augmentation, proving that arbitrary constraint families need not define matroids.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility means satisfying both displayed cardinality inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\{2\}\) and \(B=\{1,3\}\) violate matroid augmentation; therefore the feasible family is not a matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal I_G=\{F\subseteq E:(V,F)\text{ contains no cycle}\}\). Then \(\mathcal I_G\) is the independent-set family of a matroid \(M(G)\) on \(E\), called the graphic matroid of \(G\). Its circuits are precisely the edge sets of graph-theoretic cycles, including a loop as a one-element cycle and two parallel edges as a two-element cycle. Its bases are the maximal forests of \(G\); if \(G\) is connected, these are exactly its spanning trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graphic matroid has graph edges as elements and forests as independent sets; its circuits are graph cycles and its bases are maximal forests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphic Matroid Structure and Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cycle matroids and records their circuits, bases, rank, minor operations, regularity, and excluded-minor characterization among regular matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\), the forests form the independent sets of a matroid \(M(G)\). Its circuits are the graph cycles, its bases are the maximal forests, and for every \(F\subseteq E\), \(r_{M(G)}(F)=|V|-\kappa(V,F)\). Matroid deletion and contraction correspond to edge deletion and contraction. An oriented incidence matrix represents \(M(G)\) over every field, so every graphic matroid is regular. A regular matroid is graphic if and only if it has neither \(M(K_5)^*\) nor \(M(K_{3,3})^*\) as a minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forests of a graph form its cycle matroid. Its circuits are graph cycles, its bases are maximal forests, and an edge set has rank equal to the number of vertices minus the number of induced components. Edge deletion and contraction agree with matroid deletion and contraction. Graphic matroids are regular, and among regular matroids they are characterized by excluding the dual cycle matroids of K5 and K3,3.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(G)\text{ is a regular matroid},\quad r_{M(G)}(F)=|V|-\kappa(V,F)
